findings: For the 23 EXECUTED records, status functions as process-state evidence that a bounded patch workflow ran; it does not by itself declare a live authority transition.
For the 2 PASS records, PASS is bounded validation or gate success evidence plus implementation evidence, not an explicit authority grant.
No C03 patch record carries an explicit authority_effect field, so current records do not explicitly promote the patch record itself into live authority.
Generic registry lookup still returns the patch record itself because the current fallback reasons over registry patch-record presence rather than over lifecycle-completion semantics.

separated_dimensions.lifecycle_state: All 25 remain typed as proposal in the Q3 queue with no explicit recorded post-execution lifecycle transition.
separated_dimensions.execution_state: Observed as EXECUTED for 23 records and PASS-like completion for 2 records.
separated_dimensions.validation_state: Observed as validation.result=pass script results for 23 records and validation_results pass bundles for 2 records.
separated_dimensions.implementation_state: 23 records summarize results without explicit file lists; 2 records record concrete files_changed bundles.
separated_dimensions.authority_effect: Absent or untyped for all 25 records.
separated_dimensions.surface_authority: Where any affected live surface has an explicit role, it resolves independently through existing role-aware machinery rather than through the patch record.

executed_only_family.finding: The executed-only records mostly summarize registry, textbook, or SSOT maintenance effects, but they do not expose an explicit authority-bearing implementation surface through the patch record itself.
executed_only_family.authority_conclusion: Execution and pass validation script results are non-authoritative evidence unless a separate live role resolves an affected surface.

mechanism_1.name: EXECUTED_PROPOSAL_RECORD_WITH_MISSING_TRANSITION
mechanism_1.description: Execution completed and validation.result=pass is recorded, but no explicit lifecycle transition moves the record out of proposal typing, and generic lookup still returns the patch record itself.

mechanism_2.name: PASS_RECORD_WITH_INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_EFFECTS
mechanism_2.description: PASS validation bundles and concrete files_changed evidence exist, but they describe bounded implementation and verification work rather than patch-record authority, and current lookup still returns the patch record itself.

unsafe_generalizations: Do not treat EXECUTED as an automatic live-authority state.
Do not treat PASS or validation success as authority promotion.
Do not treat applied implementation effects as proof that the patch record itself is authoritative.
Do not merge the 23 executed-only records with the 2 PASS bundle records into one enforcement patch without separating their denser implementation semantics.

selected_next_component.root_problem: Executed patch records remain proposal-typed and still resolve as live registry authority candidates because execution completion is not yet bounded away from live authority lookup.
selected_next_component.selection_reason: This 23-item executed-only family is semantically cleaner than the 2 PASS bundle records. It can be addressed by an execution-state-is-not-live-authority boundary without first deciding how concrete files_changed and validation_results bundles should interact with independently operative implementation surfaces.
explicit_pre_resolution_proof_path: Each member still resolves allow through generic registry authority lookup.
Each member records status=EXECUTED plus validation.result=pass but no explicit authority_effect and no explicit lifecycle transition.
No existing helper currently excludes EXECUTED records from generic live lookup.
explicit_post_resolution_proof_path: Generic live lookup would defer executed proposal records unless an explicit lifecycle transition or separate governed role makes them live-eligible.
Each member could then be re-audited individually to determine whether any item-specific ambiguity remains.
selected_next_component.why_not_pass_bundle_first: The two PASS records are smaller by count but riskier because they contain concrete implementation bundles and at least one explicitly role-typed affected surface, so a premature shared boundary could suppress legitimate independently governed operational surfaces.
